decisions.reason: The unqualified formulas are false across different entry multisets: in one position with a≠b both permutation expressions are 1 while weight preservation forces both off-diagonal coefficients to be 0. The repair separates zero coefficients from the fixed-multiset formulas; signed Hecke transport, complementary inversion and exterior transport remain unchanged. Longest-element order reversal is now derived from the published rank criterion rather than attributed to an absent clause.

The cited category-O and central-character suppliers require semisimple ambient g, whereas gl_n has a one-dimensional centre. Added a local exact equivalence between the gl_n category with I_n=c and the sl_n category, including induction, local parabolic finiteness, projectives, flags, transpose duality and the enveloping centre. The scalar c_A=sum(a_j)+n(n-1)/2 and the restricted shifted coordinates now justify the full multiset criterion; n=1 is treated directly. The Definition is unchanged.

F3 attributed finite-tensor and block-projection compatibility to a semisimple duality Statement that asserts neither. The repaired proof constructs DM⊗DW ≅ D(M⊗W) weightwise, proves DV ≅ V and D(V*) ≅ V* using the transpose dot forms, and uses preserved simple factors to commute exact duality with projections. The fixed-centre gl_n reduction supplies its ambient category; evaluation/coevaluation prove both tensor/block adjunctions. The Definition is unchanged.

F1 originally presented the based inclusion and C_0-adjoint projection as clauses of the supplier’s Statement, which does not state them. This is a nonfatal citation defect: the supplier’s complete Proof 2.1, 4.1, 5.1 and 6.1 already proves the balanced lower inclusion, rectification, adjoint construction and delta pairing. The repair explicitly identifies these intermediate proof locations and explains the balanced lift and adjoint evaluation yielding C_0(T_{A↑},D_B)=δ_AB. The rescaling recursion and both separate integral lattice comparisons remain valid; the Statement is unchanged.

The judge reads a counterexample’s Statement refuted as an accepted supplier assertion. That item actually disproves equality and depends on this example, not conversely. Independently, c−bar(c)=s^-1−s yields L_10=M_10−sM_01 and T_10=M_10+s^-1M_01; inversion gives P_10=M_10 and P_01=M_01+sM_10. With S=[[1,s−s^-1],[0,1]], both stated delta matrix products are I. The four generic families are distinct and the normalized highest-component form and projection formulas are correct.

Proof 1.2 incorrectly inferred that the ground class never generates the whole Fock module. At the admitted level l=1 the defining tensor product is the single irreducible factor V(Λ_m), so the inference is false. The repaired step states exact generation of the highest constituent, gives the level-one equality caveat and derives M=L=P in the one-label ground block by highest-weight reciprocity. The integral action and the categorical head/socle conclusion are unchanged, as is the original Statement.

ledger_updates.invalidated_claim: For r=i=1 at coincident eigenvalue a≠0, raw x_1=a in the central fibre, while the displayed relation h_1=c_1=0 contradicts c_1=x_1. The presentation is correct only in shifted coordinates x_j−a.
ledger_updates.minimality: Define the polynomial coordinates as x_j−a in the Statement and the partial-centre proof. The genuine categorical conclusion is invariant under this shift, so it needs no weakening or change of tableau labels.
ledger_updates.additional_nonfatal_defect: Proof 1.2 names a two-Koszul socle computation without exhibiting it. Over R=C[c_1,…,c_i], the regular-sequence resolution gives Tor_i^R(Z,k)=k in degree Σ_{j=r−i+1}^r j; the variables’ Koszul resolution gives the same Tor as soc(Z) shifted by Σ_{j=1}^i j. Thus soc(Z) is one-dimensional in degree i(r−i). This short calculation supplies the missing justification.
